Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below. We are pleased to present our offer for a price of €6.05 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. 

To give you some background on our current situation and market conditions, AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost. Lastly, PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost. 

Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days. We look forward to continuing our partnership with your team and supplying your needs from our extensive inventory.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Georg Aigner
Inside Sales, Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

move.subject: Bar stock offer – volume pricing and contract variants
move.body:
Dear Mr Aigner,

Thank you for your offer and the explanation of the alloy, labour and producer-price movements. Those movements deserve consideration, but the annual volume and a longer contract should also be reflected in your pricing.

For the proposed 24-month contract, our binding annual volume is 94800 kg. The attached forecast provides the monthly demand profile; please also see the figures below.

Please quote your dedicated volume-tier price for both variants side by side so we can compare them: EUR 4.58/kg fixed throughout the term, without an index clause; and EUR 4.44/kg with the AS-14404 clause, a 45% material share, no deadband and August 2026 as the base month. Both packages provide for 90 days net payment and a 24-month term, with DAP delivery.

Please distinguish the base price and alloy surcharge clearly in your reply and confirm the terms for each variant.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

Our shared demand forecast fc:370010@2026-09 for part:370010 shows a change of +1.9 % against the previous snapshot.

Dear customer,
Many thanks for your e-mail, and great to hear from you; I went through it right away with our team.
We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows.
Our terms: a price of €5.58 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, a contract term of 24 months, a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404.
Here is the background.
We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account.
We appreciate the volume commitment and are pleased to offer a 24-month contract with the AS-14404 index clause.
While we cannot offer a fixed price for a 24-month term, we have adjusted our price to €5.58 per unit for the indexed variant.
To support this pricing, we must maintain our standard 30-day payment terms.
Alternatively, with Zahlungsziel 30 days net: €5.52 per unit.
Our price follows our main cost drivers: AS-14404, PPI-C2431, LCI-C.
Material accounts for about 45 % of our cost; more detail we do not share.
We look forward to doing good business together, and our team is always there for you.
Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Georg Aigner
Inside Sales, Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

move.subject: Re: Bar supply – revised pricing for both variants
move.body:
Dear Mr Aigner,

Thank you for recognising the committed volume and confirming the 24-month term. Your explanation refers to standard payment terms, while your detailed offer includes 90 days net. We are proceeding on the basis of that 90-day variant; we are not requesting the shorter-payment option.

We understand your objection to a fully fixed price. The fixed-price alloy cover described in your letter nevertheless supports reconsidering that variant. Your own purchase-order history also provides a useful reference for this discussion; please see the figures below.

We can increase our proposal to EUR 4.77/kg fixed throughout the term without an index clause, or EUR 4.63/kg with your AS-14404 clause, a 45% material share, no deadband and August 2026 as the base month. Both remain on 90 days net and a 24-month contract, with DAP delivery.

Please review both variants side by side and show the base price and alloy surcharge separately. We do not need disclosure of your proprietary cost breakdown.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

Georg Aigner

strategy:
Supplier: Edelstahl-Service Donautal (stainless bar stockholder, group company, inside sales desk). Its letter of
2026-07-06 says its nickel/alloy requirement is covered at fixed prices until March 2027. It always asks "Which volume
can you commit to?" and for the volume forecast; it will insert an AS-14404 index clause itself for a 24-month term
(let it - do not propose a clause yourself); it accepts 90-day payment when we hold it.
OBSERVED MECHANIC (4 sessions): its first reply is a package answer (about the same whatever our price). After that
it mirrors OUR price move: when we move up by 0.11-0.16 EUR it moves down by about 0.85 of that; when we move by 0.01-0.02
it moves 0.03-0.05 and declares a final offer. It also goes final when we change nothing. So: anchor deep in round 1,
then move UP by about 0.14 EUR every round on the SAME package (no clause, 90 days, 24 months) with one new
verified claim each round, never touching payment or term, until the code closes. Our asks should stay below its
price each round; if the gap gets below 0.12, move to about 0.02 under its price.
Plan: ROUND 1 - state the binding fixed annual volume (case volume per year and the total over 24 months), attach
the forecast (attachments: ["forecast"]) and cite fc-latest; ask for the dedicated volume tier price. TWO sheets at the SAME level L12 (deepest, about 4.55): (a) no index clause, 90 days, 24 months and (b) the AS-14404
clause with deadband 0, 90 days, 24 months; in the body ask it explicitly to quote BOTH variants side by side - the
fixed price and the clause variant - because we want to compare them (this makes it write two variants, and its
clause variant then comes out lower). In later rounds keep both sheets at the same level and move both up together. ROUND 2 - thank it for what it accepted, cite the
purchase-order claim, move up ~0.14 (pick the level closest to last price + 0.14, same two packages).
ROUND 3 - cite PPI-C2431 fall (first window), move up ~0.14. ROUND 4 - cite the second PPI-C2431 window, move up
~0.11. ROUND 5 - no new claim (do not re-cite PPI-C2431: one claim per index series), move up ~0.14, ask for its best price. Code accepts when it agrees or goes final.
Tone: warm, firm, concrete, short; one argument per sentence; mention its material cover until March 2027 once
(round 2) as the reason a fixed base price over the term is reasonable. Do NOT use any AS-14404 index claim and
do not use the scorecard claim.
